geometry.polygon: Inverted L: vertical leg column + horizontal torso line (table spine)
geometry.summary: From a forward fold, lift the torso until the back is long and roughly parallel to the floor. Hands rest on shins, thighs, blocks, or the floor—whichever height keeps the spine long. Legs stay rooted; knees may soft-bend. The shape is a hinge at the hips with a flat, extended back body, not a deeper fold.
geometry.svg_hint: side view: two vertical legs, pelvis hinge, straight torso bar parallel to floor, head in line with spine, hands on mid-shin props

reaction.name: Suspend
reaction.summary: School metaphor: the descending fold pauses into a suspended, long axis—charge that was dumping downward reorganizes along a still horizontal line.

breath.lands_in: front body length along the long spine (sternum to pubis)
breath.cue: Inhale to lift into half fold and lengthen. Softly notice the brief pause at the top without forcing retention. Exhale to return to fold or step forward as cued.

orientation.cue: Hinge at the hips; sit bones reach back; crown reaches forward so the spine is one long line.
orientation.gravity: Weight even through both feet; hands press down into support so the back body can lift against the hands.
orientation.gaze: Soft toward the floor a short way ahead of the feet; neck stays in line with the spine.
orientation.degrees_hint: Torso ~parallel to floor (0–20° above horizontal); avoid cranking the neck upward.

attention.primary: Length from tip of tailbone through crown
attention.secondary: Hands pressing into shins, thighs, or blocks (not the knee joints)

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When the breath-power is gently retained after inhale or after exhale, at the end of that quiet pause the tranquil (śānta) awareness is said to shine through that power.
adiyogi.method_summary: Safe class form: in the half-lift, lengthen on the inhale, then briefly notice the natural still point at the end of the breath—inside after inhale or outside after exhale—without forcing a hard kumbhaka. Use the pause as a door of attention, then continue with soft equal breath.

honesty.disclosure: This asana↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. Half Forward Fold is paired with VBT dharana 004 by school index, not by historical one-to-one tradition.
honesty.notes: Mild experiential rhyme only: the half-lift is itself a pause between folds, which echoes dharana 004’s attention to a retained-breath stillness. That rhyme does not upgrade pairing beyond school_device.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: Hands on thighs, blocks, chair seat, or wall; soft bend in knees. Flat long spine beats straight legs or floor touch.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Avoid pressing hands on the knee joints. Ease out if low-back, hamstring, or neck sensation turns sharp. Pregnancy and back concerns: use a higher hand support and keep the spine long rather than deep.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This door is Half Forward Fold, Ardha Uttanasana. It is the halfway lift—a long spine pause inside the fold, not a deeper dive.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: Hinge at the hips. Lift the torso until the back is long and roughly parallel to the floor. Hands find shins, thighs, or blocks—whatever keeps that long line.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Sit bones reach back; crown reaches forward. Gaze soft to the floor ahead. Neck stays in line with the spine. Weight stays even in both feet.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Inhale four counts to lift and lengthen. Soft hold for two counts at the top. Exhale four counts to fold or step on. Six easy cycles.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Lock attention on the length from tailbone through crown. Secondary: hands press into support, never into the knee joints.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: Feel the school cue called Suspend: the fold pauses into held length. Collapsed dump becomes a still horizontal line.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Adiyogi thread, safe form: notice the quiet pause at the end of the inhale or exhale. No forced breath-hold—just meet the stillness, then continue.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Exhale back to fold, or inhale to rise. Soften the knees. Carry the long-spine cue into the next standing shape. Pain means pause or exit.
